label: FY27 Q1 (Jul–Sep 2026)
dateLabel: before the open, 2 Nov 2026 (with the Marvell deal)
asOf: close of $538.59 on 6 Nov 2026; $840.70 before the report (30 Oct)
headline: Revenue 2.4x in a year and a 42% margin, yet on the same day it agreed to sell itself to Marvell: the stock now tracks Marvell, 15% below the exchange value

points.t: Each LITE share becomes 4.5 Marvell shares. That was about $1,132 a share on pre-rumor prices of 28 Oct (a 24% premium), but Marvell has since fallen, so at the 6 Nov close it is worth about $635; closing is expected only in 1H 2028.
Revenue rose 137%, led by laser chips and optical circuit switches (OCS); it won a second big NPO/CPO deal backed by more than $5B of purchase commitments. Next quarter adds another ~$350M.
On deal day LITE closed at $684.40 (−18.6%), with Marvell down 12.7%. It kept falling with the AI sector to $538.59 on 6 Nov, about 15% below the exchange value.

reaction: Stock: on 2 Nov (results and the merger announced together) it closed at $684.40, down 18.6%; acquirer Marvell fell 12.7% the same day. Since then LITE has mostly tracked Marvell: on 5 Nov, as the AI sector sold off, both fell about 16–19%. Consensus from Newsquawk: EPS $4.19, revenue $1.249B (TIKR cites $4.22 EPS).

segments.title: By product type
segments.take: Both are growing fast, with Systems (transceivers and optical switches) growing more than twice as fast as Components.

rows.why: Data-center laser chips (EMLs and CW lasers for 800G/1.6T transceivers and CPO) and pump lasers (for long-haul links between data centers). Management named pump lasers as one of the biggest growth contributors.

Cloud transceivers (with improving gross margin) and optical circuit switches. OCS switches light paths with mirrors, removing electrical switches; Google was the first big user. The company says OCS could become a multi-billion-dollar annual business.

segments.note: Systems was $155M a year ago and $508M now; Components $379M a year ago and $754M now. Shares are of this quarter's revenue.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Lumentum is the light source of optical networking: laser chips inside transceivers, pump lasers for long-haul links and switches that route light directly.

items.w: 1.6T transceivers and CPO need high-power laser chips, and indium phosphide capacity is one of the industry's bottlenecks.
Management says OCS demand visibility “expanded significantly in recent months”, positioning it as a multi-billion-dollar annual business.
A second major NPO/CPO win, with purchase commitments above $5B, is a sign optics is moving inside the GPU rack.
After closing, Marvell could offer everything from electrical chips (DSPs, switches) to lasers and transceivers, competing with Broadcom and NVIDIA.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Buying LITE now is mostly buying Marvell stock plus a deal spread. The business's own growth sets the fallback value if the deal fails.

items.w: At Marvell's $141.20 on 6 Nov, each share is worth about $635; LITE closed at $538.59, a spread of about 15% (not high annualized, given the wait until 1H 2028).
The Q2 midpoint of $1.6B adds about $350M q/q, more than the whole company's quarterly revenue two years ago.
Q2 operating margin is guided to 45–46%, against 19% a year ago.
It needs both shareholder votes and approvals in several countries (optics is sensitive, and China's review is a common uncertainty). Termination fees: $5.8B on Marvell's side, $2.9B on Lumentum's.
Marvell's stock falling further; regulators blocking the deal; industry indium phosphide oversupply cutting laser-chip prices; customers moving orders to rivals during the merger.

valuation.take: On the business alone it's about 45 times trailing non-GAAP earnings and about 22 times next quarter's guide annualized. But after the merger, LITE's price is set mainly by 4.5x Marvell's stock and the odds the deal closes.

forward.title: Next quarter annualized

head: Case
Value per share

scenarios.note: Bear: the deal breaks, LITE is standalone again and optics cools, with standalone FY28 EPS about $25 (below the $35.7 consensus, assuming laser-chip price cuts) × 15; base: the deal closes with Marvell at its 6 Nov price; bull: the deal closes with Marvell back at its 28 Oct price, both = 4.5 × Marvell's price ($141.20 / $251.60). The time until closing is not discounted. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: base and bull = 4.5 × Marvell's price; bear = standalone FY28 EPS × 15
pricezone.why: The price sits at the top of the zone: buying at $539, the base case gains about 18% and the bear case loses about 30%, a reward/risk of about 0.6; at the $495 midpoint it is about 1.2, and at the $450 low end about 2.5. This zone is really a price for “Marvell plus deal risk”: if you don't like Marvell, you shouldn't like LITE.

history.title: Against its own past

history.note: From 2H 2025 the multiple rose from about 4x to 27x; it's about 15x now. After the merger this history matters less. Calculated from SEC XBRL quarterly revenue, diluted shares and Nasdaq quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Non-GAAP operating margin
cash.note: Cash and short-term investments fell $759M from last quarter, and the release summary doesn't explain why (part of last quarter's convertible-note conversion was cash-settled, and capacity is expanding). No dividend or buyback.

valuation.next: Next report around early February 2027; merger votes and regulatory progress will be announced separately.

changes.now: Merger agreement signed on 1 Nov; CEO Michael Hurlston will join Marvell's board.

insider.title: Effective trades 30 days around the report
insider.text: Insider Flow recorded no open-market buy or sell filings for Lumentum in the 30 days before the report (10/3–11/2). After the deal, executives signed tax reimbursement agreements (covering change-of-control taxes), which are not trades. The 30 days after the report update daily with Insider Flow; see the Insider Flow page.
